narrator.base: Voice: a warm Indian woman narrating a short documentary, Indian English accent. Pacing: unhurried and clear, with natural pauses. Say Hindi words written in Devanagari the Hindi way, and say 'Saathi' as the Hindi word 'saa-thee' (friend).

scammer.base: Voice: a young Indian man on a bad phone line, speaking Hindi. Panicked, breathless and pleading, rushing his words as if he is hurt and scared.

rahul.base: Voice: a young Indian man speaking Hindi to his mother on the phone. Gentle, warm and reassuring, a little emotional.

sunita.base: Voice: an Indian woman in her sixties speaking Hindi on the phone. Deeply relieved, her voice soft and shaking, close to tears.

lines.text: मम्मी, मैं राहुल… मेरा एक्सीडेंट हो गया है।
अभी पचास हज़ार भेज दो। पापा को मत बताना।

lines.mood: Grave and quiet, with a sense of urgency.
lines.text: A scam like this works in the two minutes between the call and the transfer.

lines.mood: Quiet resolve, a small lift of hope.
lines.text: असली है. Built for exactly those two minutes.
One tap. Sunita opens the button her son added to her home screen, and presses it. Nothing to read, nothing to fill in.
Two calls start at the same moment. साथी calls Sunita, and her son, Rahul, gets a rescue call.

lines.mood: Tense and present, like a thriller.
lines.text: Sunita is in Lucknow. Rahul is in Bengaluru. Both phones ring together.
Sunita tells साथी what happened, in her own words.
Her story is pushed straight into Rahul's live call.
And Rahul? He says he never called.
And the verdict lands in Sunita's call, word for word, in about thirty seconds.
Rahul is asked to call her too.
So he does. The scammer gets nothing.
माँ, मैं बिल्कुल ठीक हूँ। वो कॉल मेरा नहीं था।
भगवान का शुक्र है।
And if it really is him? Rahul says the family word. Only the backend checks it, and then साथी tells her the call is real.
A caller claiming to be the police? A fixed warning plays, and Rahul hears at once.
Money already sent? साथी tells her to call nineteen-thirty, the cybercrime helpline, straight away.
Still stuck on the scammer's call? Rahul is told to ring her himself.
Family not answering? She can ask साथी to try again, and she does.
Made for her. One button. No forms, no menus, nothing to learn.
Her language, in her own script. Hindi, English, Hinglish, and ten more Indian languages.
Bigger text in one tap. And the button never gets smaller than a palm.
Every control has a name, so a screen reader can tell her exactly what it does.
The family sets it up, one question per screen. One phone can protect a mother, a father, and a sister.
And it can't be talked into paying.
The family word stays secret. साथी never asks for an OTP, never promises money back, and her safety lines can't be talked over.
There is no digital arrest in Indian law. If money has gone, call nineteen-thirty, right away.
Under the hood: two Bolna agents and a small backend, pushing events into live calls.

lines.mood: Warm, hopeful and moved, slowing down at the end.
lines.text: असली है. One tap, before a parent pays.
